current.text: He signed a two-year deal with Chicago with a team option in the second year.
He is in Chicago's projected starting five with Josh Giddey, Matas Buzelis, Caleb Wilson and Nick Claxton.
Nikola Vucevic and Coby White left Chicago, which frees up usage.
He is the Bulls' main off-ball shooter on a team that lacks shooting.
Experts expect him to lead the Bulls in usage, in the high 20s, because the other scorers are low-usage players and no one is coming in to take his shots.

Trade risk is high. His contract looks built for a trade and the front office signs older players hoping to trade them. A trade to a better team where he is the third option would cut his usage and collapse his value, possibly before the fantasy playoffs.
Experts see him as a pick around 80th overall, in round 7 or 8, with more downside than upside. A rank around 65, as on ESPN, expects too much.
In auction, Josh values him at 6 to 7 USD. He went for 3 USD in a mock auction, which Josh called basically the best pick of the draft.
Chicago projects as a bad team, likely bottom 10 (Hayes predicts 32 wins), and should play a fast, up-tempo style.
Chicago plays 10 games in our fantasy playoffs (3-3-4) and has 15 back-to-backs, one below the maximum.

durable.text: His fantasy value depends entirely on high usage. He puts up big numbers when he has the ball to himself and fades when he shares it with a good player, even while shooting around 40% from three.
He is a points and threes player. He gives little in rebounds, assists and blocks.
He is good at getting to the free throw line and shoots a solid FT%.
His efficiency is decent, but Hayes does not see his 20-plus points on about 15 shots as tremendous value.
Over the last two to three months of 2025-26 he shot 33% from three and under 80% from the line, and fell outside the top 150.
Because he only adds scoring, an off shooting stretch or season hurts his value badly.
He is not a point guard and does not dribble well.

note: Powell is a points and threes scorer (21.9 PTS and 2.8 3PM projected) whose value depends on staying Chicago's top usage option. The experts agree he is worth about 80th overall and 6 to 7 USD. That makes Yahoo's 2.4 USD average cost a bargain, while a price near ESPN's rank 67 (4.6 USD) or our 8 USD from last season is full price. He fits any build that wants scoring and threes. Early in the season, watch his usage share and three-point shooting, and follow trade rumors before the 2027-03-04 deadline, because a trade to a contender would gut his value before our playoffs.
